findings.title: Shard-split queries are now interpolated twice (once here, again in runSplitQuery)
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables and then passes those already-interpolated targets to splitQueriesByStreamShard, which builds sub-requests handed to runSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163). runSplitQuery now interpolates the same targets again via datasource.applyTemplateVariables (querySplitting.ts:299), once per shard group and once per retry — the updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' even asserts 5 calls of applyTemplateVariables for a single query (1 here + 4 inside runSplitQuery). This is only safe if template interpolation is idempotent: any variable whose interpolated value itself contains '$'-prefixed text (e.g. regex-valued variables, a value containing a literal '$' followed by an existing variable name) will be substituted a second time on the already-resolved string, silently corrupting the executed query. The shard selector inserted by interpolateShardingSelector is also fed back through variable substitution. Interpolation should happen exactly once — either drop the map in runShardSplitQuery and let runSplitQuery own it, or skip re-interpolation in runSplitQuery when invoked from the shard path.

findings.title: $__range exclusion in querySupportsSplitting is evaluated after interpolation and may no longer trigger
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting's `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` check now runs on expressions that have already been through datasource.applyTemplateVariables (the map at line 299 happens before the partition at line 300). If LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables resolves the Loki range variables ($__range, $__range_s, $__range_ms — it does resolve other built-ins such as $__auto, as the new tests demonstrate), the check can never match anymore, so $__range queries will now be split into 1-day chunks. That is a significant behavior change: each chunk would evaluate the full-range lookback window (a 30-day $__range split into 30 chunks scans roughly 30x the data), and if Loki clips range-vector lookback at the sub-query start, the results near chunk boundaries would be wrong. The comment above the check ("interpolated on the backend with the split timeRange") also no longer describes the new flow, since interpolation now happens on the frontend first. Please verify whether applyTemplateVariables resolves the range variables: if it does, the guard is dead code and the split of $__range queries must be an intended, tested behavior (comment updated accordingly); if it does not, make it explicit that this check still relies on $__range surviving frontend interpolation.
